books.section: Progressive Era and World War I (1900-1920)

stimulus.text: In 1919 President Wilson asked the Senate to ratify the Treaty of Versailles, which included American membership in the League of Nations. Senator Henry Cabot Lodge, who led the opposition, insisted on reservations that would keep Congress in control of any American military commitment abroad. The Senate rejected the treaty, with and without Lodge's reservations, and the United States never joined the League.

stem: The United States refused to join the League of Nations yet hosted the Washington Naval Conference in 1921. That combination best shows which of the following?

options.text: A complete withdrawal from all world affairs
options.misconception: Hosting a disarmament conference and signing treaties is not withdrawal.
Collective security means promising to defend others; the Senate refused exactly that.

options.text: Support for the League in all but name
options.misconception: The United States never joined the League, in name or in fact.

rationales.A: Background from the books: the United States hosted the conference and signed three treaties there.
rationales.B: The United States led disarmament talks while refusing the League's binding promises.
rationales.C: Background from the books: collective security requires a promise to defend others, which the Senate rejected.
rationales.D: Background from the books: the United States stayed out of the League entirely.
rationales.general:
1. The passage shows the Senate refusing League membership in 1919.
2. Two years later the United States hosted the Washington Naval Conference and signed the Five-Power Treaty.
3. The treaties limited ships but promised no troops and set up no enforcement.
4. Refusing the League while leading disarmament is one pattern: engagement without entanglement.
Remember: a country can lead talks and still refuse promises.
